headline: Local IT Professional Attempts To Recreate 1972 Diplomatic Breakthrough By Ordering Butter Chicken Tacos At Neighborhood Food Court
body:
Sumit Verma, a 34-year-old software architect, spent three hours yesterday meticulously arranging a plate of butter chicken tacos in his office cafeteria, claiming the dish was a 'deliberate strategic overture' designed to reconcile his department’s ongoing dispute over project deadlines. Inspired by the elaborate historical nuances of recent high-profile state dinners, Verma insisted that the fusion of North Indian gravy and Tex-Mex shells served as a symbolic bridge between his team's legacy code and the modern agile methodology they refuse to adopt.

'I didn't just order lunch; I curated a diplomatic moment,' Verma told coworkers while adjusting his napkin to ensure it mirrored the formal aesthetics of a 1970s summit. 'By presenting these tacos to the lead project manager, I am effectively inviting him to a new era of cross-functional cooperation, much like the historic toasts that shaped global relations five decades ago. The chutney on the side represents our commitment to open-source transparency.'

The project manager, who spent the duration of the 'summit' checking his watch and wondering if he could expense the lunch as a business meeting, reportedly accepted a taco but remained skeptical of the geopolitical implications. 'I thought we were just grabbing a quick bite before the afternoon stand-up,' he noted, wiping orange sauce from his sleeve. 'I’m not entirely sure if this is a peace treaty or just an extremely messy way to ask for an extension on the user testing documentation.'
caption: Sumit truly believes his lunch choice has shifted the trajectory of his office. How far would you go to avoid a difficult meeting? #OfficeDiplomacy #ButterChickenTacos #CorporateLife #CorporateCulture (satire)
